chains.title: Why colonial agriculture stagnated
steps: Colonial land settlement: the zamindari system
Zamindars must pay fixed revenue by fixed dates or lose their rights
Zamindars care only about collecting rent; the profit goes to them
Little is done to improve farming
Low productivity: stagnation and, not infrequently, unusual deterioration

chains.title: The two-fold motive and the fall of handicrafts
steps: Two-fold motive: India as raw-material exporter and market for British goods
India's world-famous handicrafts decline
Artisans lose work; locally made goods vanish from markets
Cheap British imports fill the demand

chains.title: Export surplus and the drain of wealth
steps: India exports primary products and imports finished goods
A large export surplus
It pays for an office in Britain, British wars and invisible imports
No gold or silver flows in: the drain of Indian wealth

chains.title: Railways and commercialisation
steps: Railways carry cash crops to the ports
Commercialisation: a small section of farmers switch to cash crops
Village economies lose their self-sufficiency

chains.title: Box 1.3: the Suez Canal tightens Britain's grip
steps: 1869: the Suez Canal opens in Egypt
Ships no longer need to sail around Africa
Transport costs fall; access to the Indian market gets easier
British control over India's foreign trade intensifies
